facts: Lutyens’s 1928 pavilion has three Doric bays, vaulted interior, stepped central attic and circular drum, pedimented arch entrances, bronze plaque banks, five steps at each end and checkerboard stone paving.
Maufe’s 1955 sunken lawn has 8-foot Portland stone and bronze walls, stone paved walks, oak seating, a bronze compass, paired entrance pylons and a Stone of Remembrance on a stepped base.

record: Commonwealth War Graves Commission visitor sheet hosted by the Australian DVA
facts: The two sections were unveiled on 12 December 1928 and 5 November 1955 and commemorate the crews of merchant ships and fishing vessels.
